text:
anya: noticed a sustained p99 jump on hosted-api-us-west over the last ~5m, p95 elevated too. queue depth up on the batcher and a bunch of requests falling back to the slower kernel variant. investigation pls :eyes:
sam: saw that. is this correlated with any deploys?
zane: no deploys in the last hour, infra metrics show a sudden increase in small-ish requests (avg tokens ~18) and a few tenants with high QPS. could be noisy tenants triggering small-batch inefficiency.
kat: can we confirm KV cache eviction rates? if hot prefixes are getting evicted we'll see priming costs + kernel fallback. run profile on kvcache hit ratio for affected instances.
anya: grabbing traces now, hitting the nodes that report >200ms tail. infra-bot: collected logs from node-34 and node-37, uploaded to /tmp/diag/1718801234.tar.gz
sam: pasted relevant excerpt from runtime logs:
```
[2024-06-12T15:20:14Z] batcher: queue_depth=42, max_batch=64, avg_batch=6
[2024-06-12T15:20:15Z] kernel-selector: chosen=quant_fast, fallback=slow_dense, reason=kv_cache_miss
[2024-06-12T15:20:15Z] kvcache: evictions=128, hit_rate=0.62
[2024-06-12T15:20:15Z] rate-limiter: tenant=acme-corp, throttled=false, burst_used=0.85
```
zane: hit_rate 0.62 is lower than expected for these traffic patterns. eviction spikes line up with the p99s. suspect kvcache churn from a tenant that cycles many short prompts.
kat: can we temporarily pin kernel selection to prefer the dense kernel for these nodes to avoid fallback churn while we investigate? need a quick mitigation.
ops: we can push a kernel policy to the pool, but it'll raise avg latency a bit; want to try in canary first.
anya: +1 to canary. start with node-37 only. infra-bot: scheduling canary rollout to node-37 now.
infra-bot: canary applied to node-37: kernel_policy=prefer_dense, ttl=15m
sam: after apply, tail dropped from ~420ms to ~210ms on node-37 within 90s. queue depth also came down ~25%.
zane: good signal. next step: profile KV cache keys churn with sampling (enable kvcache-sampler on affected pool) for 10m, collect histograms of prefix reuse. command below:
```
# enable sampler
curl -X POST https://internal-api/redwood/runtime/pools/hosting-uwest/actions -d '{"action":"enable_kvcache_sampler","duration":"600s"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $DIAG'
```
kat: also fetch `perf` output around kernel-selection hot paths and the batcher thread. low-overhead traces would help (e.g., eBPF sampling).
anya: doing both. putting a note in the incident doc with correlating graphs. ops: is there a quick rate limit rule we can apply to noisy tenants?
ops: yes, we can opt-in per-tenant shaping to smooth bursts. prefer to rely on trial policy first (soft cap) to avoid throttling legitimate traffic.
zane: if sampler shows lots of new prefixes per second, remediation is a longer-term change: increase kvcache size for that tenant class or adjust prefix hashing to reduce false eviction.
anya: agreed. immediate plan: 1) keep kernel policy canary for 15m, 2) collect kvcache sampler + perf samples, 3) apply soft shaping to top noisy tenant if churn persists, 4) follow-up with model/usage owner to reduce tiny prompt blast if possible.
sam: adding retention note - attach profiler tar and kvcache histograms to the ticket: INF-4521.
ops: will monitor and escalate if p99 rises again. thanks team :thumbsup:
